title: D-Day: the Normandy landings

where.name: Omaha Beach, Normandy
where.note: Marker placed at Omaha Beach, one of five landing beaches along about 50 miles of the Normandy coast.

summary: Allied forces landed on five beaches in Normandy in the largest amphibious invasion in history, beginning the liberation of north-west Europe from German occupation.
description: Just after midnight on 6 June 1944, some 23,400 airborne troops landed behind the Normandy beaches to protect the flanks of the invasion. From 6:30 a.m., after naval bombardment and air attacks, assault troops came ashore: Americans at Utah and Omaha, British at Gold and Sword, and Canadians at Juno.
Nearly 160,000 Allied troops landed in Normandy on D-Day. American troops suffered the heaviest casualties at Omaha Beach, where more than 34,000 came ashore.
context: Codenamed Operation Overlord, the landings marked the start of a long and costly campaign to liberate north-west Europe. The Imperial War Museums describe D-Day as the largest combined naval, air and land operation in the history of warfare.

facts.text: About 23,400 airborne troops landed early on 6 June.
Nearly 160,000 Allied troops landed on D-Day.
By nightfall the Allies had suffered over 10,300 casualties — killed, wounded and missing — about 2,400 of them at Omaha Beach.

uncertain.text: Casualty figures for D-Day alone cannot be stated exactly; the National WWII Museum gives 'over 10,300' Allied casualties by nightfall.
